content: The co-administration of Welchol and a statin (atorvastatin, lovastatin, or simvastatin) was evaluated in three clinical studies, demonstrating an additive reduction in LDL-C levels. In the atorvastatin study, the mean baseline LDL-C was 184 mg/dL, with a range of 156 to 236 mg/dL. In the lovastatin study, the mean baseline LDL-C was 171 mg/dL, ranging from 115 to 247 mg/dL. In the simvastatin study, the mean baseline LDL-C was 188 mg/dL, with a range of 148 to 352 mg/dL. The addition of 8 g of Welchol resulted in an additional 8% to 16% reduction in LDL-C levels compared to statin therapy alone. Across all three studies, the combination of Welchol and any given dose of statin therapy achieved statistically superior LDL-C reductions compared to either Welchol or the statin alone. The effect of Welchol in combination with fenofibrate was assessed in 122 patients with mixed hyperlipidemia (Fredrickson Type IIb). Inclusion criteria required LDL-C levels of ≥115 mg/dL and triglyceride (TG) levels between 150 mg/dL and 749 mg/dL. Patients were randomized to receive either 8 g of Welchol or placebo for six weeks in a double-blind treatment phase. The overall mean LDL-C at the start of randomized treatment was 144 mg/dL. The study results demonstrated that Welchol significantly reduced plasma levels of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, total cholesterol (TC), and Apo B, while significantly increasing HDL-C levels. A moderate, non-statistically significant increase in TG levels was observed compared to placebo. In a separate study involving pediatric patients (ages 10 to 17 years) with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (heFH), participants were either on a stable dose of an FDA-approved statin with LDL-C >130 mg/dL or were statin-naïve with LDL-C >160 mg/dL. This study consisted of three periods: a single-blind placebo stabilization period, an 8-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled treatment period, and an 18-week open-label treatment period. At screening, 24% of patients were on statins, while 76% were statin-naïve. The mean baseline LDL-C at Day 1 was approximately 199 mg/dL. A total of 186 patients completed the double-blind treatment period. Welchol at 8 g/day significantly decreased LDL-C, non-HDL-C, TC, and Apo B levels, while significantly increasing HDL-C levels. A moderate, non-statistically significant increase in TG levels was observed compared to placebo. At Week 26, 89% of patients (173 individuals) completed the treatment, and the results were consistent with those observed at Week 8. Welchol has also been studied for its effects in patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, both as monotherapy and in combination with metformin, sulfonylureas, and insulin.
